keywords.def: (idiom) is exactly what you want or need
not expensive; cheap enough that most people can buy it
there is only just enough money available to pay for the basics needed to live
(idiom) done while busy travelling or moving around, rather than at home
state in which your mind is fully focused, active and engaged, not dull or foggy
(idiom) do or say things which are different from most other people, because you do not mind being different

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Beth. It seems people around the world are in love with snacks!
sentences.zh: 我是 Neil。而我是 Beth。看来世界各地的人们都非常热爱零食！

sentences.en: From old favourites like popcorn and crisps to new inventions like the chocolate sandwich, snacks are big business, with an estimated $1.5 trillion a year spent globally on snacking.
sentences.zh: 从爆米花和薯片等传统挚爱，到巧克力三明治等全新发明，零食是一个庞大的产业，全球每年的零食消费额估计高达 1.5 万亿美元。

sentences.en: Let's listen as British food historian Annie Gray and Argentinian chef Barbara Oievari tell BBC World Service programme The Food Chain what they like to snack on between meals: I like salted peanuts and I love a banana – preferably together, actually.
sentences.zh: 让我们听听英国饮食史学家 Annie Gray 和阿根廷厨师 Barbara Oievari 在 BBC World Service 节目 The Food Chain 中讲述他们两餐之间喜欢吃什么零食：我喜欢咸花生，我也很喜欢香蕉——其实最好能一起吃。

sentences.en: I find that they hit the spot. My favourite snack is called 'chipa'.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它们正合我意。我最喜欢的零食叫“chipa”。

sentences.en: It's a small, round bun made with cassava, cheese, butter, milk and salt.
sentences.zh: 它是一种用木薯、奶酪、黄油、牛奶和盐做成的小圆面包。

sentences.en: Barbara's favourite snack is a cheese bread called 'chipa', while for Annie, it's the combination of peanuts and banana that hits the spot – an idiom meaning that it's exactly what you want.
sentences.zh: Barbara 最喜欢的零食是一种叫“chipa”的奶酪面包，而对 Annie 来说，花生和香蕉的搭配“正合我意”——这是一个习语，意思是这正是你想要的。

sentences.en: Neil, what's your favourite snack? Well, I want to say something healthy, but actually, you know, I really love a bag of crisps.
sentences.zh: Neil，你最喜欢的零食是什么？嗯，我想说点健康的，但实际上，你知道的，我真的很喜欢一包薯片。

sentences.en: Oh, me too! Yeah, crisps are good. Well, whatever you like to nibble on, in this episode we'll find out why we are so in love with snack food.
sentences.zh: 哦，我也是！对，薯片很好吃。嗯，不管你喜欢吃什么小吃，在本期节目中我们将探讨为什么我们如此热爱零食。

sentences.en: As usual, we'll learn some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样，我们将学习一些实用的新单词和短语。

sentences.en: And remember – you'll find all the vocabulary and a quiz on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 请记住——你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到所有的词汇和一个小测验。

sentences.en: OK. But first I have a question for you, Beth.
sentences.zh: 好的。但首先我有一个问题要问你，Beth。

sentences.en: According to a recent YouGov survey, which of the following snacks is most popular among Brits?
sentences.zh: 根据最近的一项 YouGov 调查，以下哪种零食在英国人中最受欢迎？

sentences.en: Is it: a) crisps, b) confectionary and chocolate, or c) savoury snacks and biscuits?
sentences.zh: 是：a) 薯片，b) 糖果和巧克力，还是 c) 咸味小吃和饼干？

sentences.en: Well, we both just said crisps so I'm going to say crisps.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们刚才都说了薯片，所以我猜薯片。

sentences.en: Well, we'll find out the answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们将在节目后面揭晓答案。

sentences.en: Someone with a professional interest in snacking is Christine Cochran, president of SNAC International, the trade association for the industry.
sentences.zh: Christine Cochran 是一个对零食行业有专业兴趣的人，她是行业贸易协会 SNAC International 的主席。

sentences.en: Here, Christine shares her ideas about why we love to snack with BBC World Service programme The Food Chain: A snack is an affordable luxury, so if you've had a bad day or money is tight, this is something that you can turn to, and I think that is why you see it as so popular.
sentences.zh: 在这里，Christine 在 BBC World Service 节目 The Food Chain 中分享了她对我们为什么热爱吃零食的看法：零食是一种负担得起的奢侈品，所以如果你今天过得很糟糕或者手头紧，这是你可以求助于的东西，我认为这就是为什么它如此受欢迎的原因。

sentences.en: Consumers, especially in the United States, are looking for smaller, more convenient portions.
sentences.zh: 消费者，尤其是在美国，正在寻找更小、更方便的分量。

sentences.en: They're not always going to be able to sit down and have three meals a day, right?
sentences.zh: 他们不可能总是能坐下来吃一日三餐，对吧？

sentences.en: So, they're eating on the go. And the other thing that you see is this desire for very specific functional ingredients, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，他们正在边走边吃。另一个现象是，人们渴望非常具体的特定功能成分，对吧？

sentences.en: So, mental clarity, gut health, muscle development, these sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 因此，精神清晰度、肠道健康、肌肉发育，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Again, they're nicely packaged in snack sizes.
sentences.zh: 同样，它们被精美地包装成零食分量。

sentences.en: Snacks are often seen as a little luxury, but to be successful a snack must also be affordable – an adjective meaning not expensive.
sentences.zh: 零食通常被视为一种小奢侈品，但要取得成功，零食还必须是 affordable 的——这是一个形容词，意为不贵。

sentences.en: Snacks which are cheap enough for most people to buy will sell even if money is tight – a phrase used to describe a situation where there's only just enough money to live on.
sentences.zh: 对于大多数人来说便宜到买得起的零食，即使手头紧——一个用来形容生活资金刚好够用的短语——也会畅销。

sentences.en: Thanks to snacks, today fewer people sit down to eat a proper meal.
sentences.zh: 多亏了零食，如今坐下来吃一顿正餐的人越来越少了。

sentences.en: Instead, they eat on the go. If you do something on the go, you do it while you're busy travelling or moving around, rather than at home.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们在路上吃。如果你在 on the go 做某事，你就是在忙于旅行或四处走动时做这件事，而不是在家吃。

sentences.en: Many modern snacks target a specific function.
sentences.zh: 许多现代零食的目标是特定功能。

sentences.en: For example, an energy drink might claim to improve your gut health or your mental clarity – a term describing a state of mind which is focused and engaged, not dull or foggy.
sentences.zh: 例如，功能饮料可能会宣称能改善你的肠道健康或 mental clarity——这个术语描述了一种专注、投入、而不沉闷或模糊的心智状态。

sentences.en: But not everyone is a fan of modern packaged snacks, such as the bags of crisps and chocolate bars which fill our shops.
sentences.zh: 但并不是每个人都喜欢现代包装零食，比如塞满我们商店货架的薯片和巧克力棒。

sentences.en: Originally from Argentina, Barbara Oievari, now lives in Florida, USA.
sentences.zh: Barbara Oievari 原籍阿根廷，现在住在美国佛罗里达州。

sentences.en: Here, Barbara tells BBC World Service's The Food Chain how she encourages her 9-year-old son to choose more natural snacks: Personally, I enjoy cooking and eating more natural, simpler snacks, but of course I can't swim against the current,and if my 9-year-old wants to eat the little baked snacks that have cheddar… ironically it is something baked with cheese in it, which is similar to what I enjoy – it's just the modern twist.
sentences.zh: 在这里，Barbara 在 BBC World Service 的 The Food Chain 中讲述了她如何鼓励她 9 岁的儿子选择更天然的零食：就个人而言，我喜欢烹饪和吃更天然、更简单的零食，但当然我不能逆流而上，如果我 9 岁的儿子想吃那些加了切达干酪的小烘焙零食……讽刺的是，这也是一种用奶酪烘焙的东西，这和我喜欢的东西很像——只是现代的扭转方式。

sentences.en: Barbara wants her son to eat healthy, homemade food, although he prefers modern, packaged snacks.
sentences.zh: Barbara 希望她的儿子吃健康的自制食物，尽管他更喜欢现代包装零食。

sentences.en: Barbara complains she can't swim against the current.
sentences.zh: Barbara 抱怨说她不能逆流而上。

sentences.en: The idiom swim against the current means to act differently from other people, often because you do not mind being different.
sentences.zh: 习语 swim against the current 的意思是表现得与其他人不同，通常是因为你不介意与众不同。

sentences.en: Well, Neil, all those snacks have made me hungry!
sentences.zh: 好吧，Neil，所有的零食都让我饿了！

sentences.en: Now, isn't it time to reveal the answer to your question?
sentences.zh: 现在，是不是该揭晓你那个问题的答案了？

sentences.en: Yes, it is. I asked, "According to a recent YouGov survey, which of the following snacks is the most popular amongst Brits?
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。我问过：“根据最近的一项 YouGov 调查，以下哪种零食在英国人中最受欢迎？

sentences.en: Crisps, confectionery and chocolate, or savoury snacks and biscuits." And the answer was… b) confectionery and chocolate, which 45% of Britons indulge in weekly, according to that survey.
sentences.zh: 薯片、糖果和巧克力，还是咸味小吃和饼干。”答案是……b) 糖果和巧克力，根据该调查，45% 的英国人每周都会纵情享用它们。

sentences.en: OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with the phrase hits the spot, which describes something which is exactly what you want or need.
sentences.zh: 好的。让我们回顾一下我们学过的词汇，首先是短语 hits the spot，它用来形容正好是你想要或需要的东西。

sentences.en: If something is affordable, it's cheap enough that most people have enough money to buy it.
sentences.zh: 如果某物是 affordable 的，说明它足够便宜，大多数人都有足够的钱买得起。

sentences.en: The phrase money is tight means you only have just enough money to live.
sentences.zh: 短语 money is tight 的意思是你的钱只够勉强维持生计。

sentences.en: The idiom on the go means doing things while you are busy travelling or moving around.
sentences.zh: 习语 on the go 意味着在忙于旅行或四处走动的同时做事情。

sentences.en: Mental clarity is a state in which your mind is fully focused and active, not dull or foggy.
sentences.zh: Mental clarity 是一种你的大脑高度专注和活跃、而不是沉闷或模糊的状态。

sentences.en: And finally, people who swim against the current, or the tide, do or say things differently from most other people.
sentences.zh: 最后，那些 swim against the current（或 the tide）的人，他们做的事或说的话与大多数人不同。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but why not head over to our website, bbclearningenglish.com, to try the quiz and worksheet for this episode?
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟节目又到时间了，为什么不访问我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com，来尝试这期节目的小测验和练习页呢？

sentences.en: See you again soon! Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 很快再见！再见！
